_note: 2026-08 sample audit, confirmed by refuter pass

fixes.e: Cat 6a supports 10GBASE-T to a full 100 m thanks to its 500 MHz bandwidth and tighter alien-crosstalk limits; Cat 5e tops out at 1 Gbps over that distance.
fixes._why: The old explanation credited "improved shielding", but shielding is optional in Cat 6a (U/UTP 6a fully meets 10GBASE-T at 100 m); the real enablers are 500 MHz bandwidth and ANEXT limits. Keyed answer unchanged. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category_6_cable

fixes.e: A loose or damaged video cable is the most common cause of intermittent flicker; refresh-rate and driver settings are checked next.
fixes._why: Dropped a garbled editing artifact ("In other words: and then refresh rate settings.") from the end of the explanation. Key unchanged.
